title: Resurrection Views Across the Theological Spectrum (Pt. 2) - Gary Habermas
summary: An interview transcript in which Gary Habermas discusses the scholarly spectrum on the resurrection, his citation practices, the dating of the 1 Corinthians 15 creed, and the practical/theological payoff of the resurrection. The material is almost entirely historical-apologetic and methodological; it touches the axiom system only at the edges, mainly through the general idea that evidence and testimony bear on a resurrection claim and that the resurrection has existential/practical import. It does not engage the formal axioms, definitions, or equations of the canon.

axiom_nodes.name: A1.1 — Existence
axiom_nodes.notes: The whole discussion presupposes that Jesus, Paul, and the resurrection events either occurred or did not, but the source never states or argues the bare axiom of existence.

axiom_nodes.name: A1.2 — Distinction
axiom_nodes.notes: Habermas repeatedly distinguishes believers/unbelievers, liberals/conservatives, bodily/non-bodily views, but this is ordinary categorical sorting, not an assertion of the metaphysical axiom of distinction.

axiom_nodes.name: A5.1 — Observation Requirement
axiom_nodes.notes: The interview is about eyewitness testimony and historical observation of resurrection appearances, but it does not assert the axiom that observation is required for actualization.

axiom_nodes.name: BC1 — Terminal Observer Exists
axiom_nodes.notes: God is mentioned as the one who separates wheat from tares and as the one who views people, but the source does not assert the terminal-observer boundary condition.

axiom_nodes.name: BC2 — Grace External To System
axiom_nodes.notes: Grace language appears only in the colloquial sense of giving someone grace in interpretation; no claim about grace as an external operator.

axiom_nodes.name: BC7 — Information Conservation
axiom_nodes.notes: The dating and preservation of early creeds is discussed, but not as a claim about information conservation in the formal sense.

axiom_nodes.name: BC8 — Voluntary Coupling
axiom_nodes.notes: Belief and unbelief are discussed as free scholarly stances, but the source does not assert the voluntary-coupling axiom.

axiom_nodes.name: D1.1 — Information Definition
axiom_nodes.notes: The source deals with historical information and testimony but never defines information in the canon's technical sense.

axiom_nodes.name: D5.1 — Observer Definition
axiom_nodes.notes: Eyewitnesses and scholars function as observers of evidence, but no formal observer definition is asserted.

axiom_nodes.name: D19.7 — Law VII Definition (Actualization Requirement)
axiom_nodes.notes: The resurrection is treated as an actual event that must be established by evidence, but the source does not state the actualization-requirement law.

axiom_nodes.name: LN1.2 — It From Bit
axiom_nodes.notes: The interview is about historical testimony and creedal information, not about information as ontologically prior to matter.

axiom_nodes.name: A11.1 — Moral Realism
axiom_nodes.notes: Jesus's commands to love God and neighbor are cited as practical implications, but the source does not assert moral realism as an axiom.

axiom_nodes.name: A11.2 — Coherence-Morality Identity
axiom_nodes.notes: Moral practice is discussed, but not as identical to coherence.

axiom_nodes.name: T11.1 — Virtue As High Phi
axiom_nodes.notes: Love of God and neighbor are mentioned as commands, but not framed in terms of integrated information or Phi.

axiom_nodes.name: T12.1 — Heaven As High-Phi Attractor
axiom_nodes.notes: Heaven is mentioned in a joke about who will be there, but not as a high-Phi attractor.

axiom_nodes.name: T12.2 — Hell As Low-Phi Attractor
axiom_nodes.notes: Hell is mentioned only in a colloquial aside, not as a low-Phi attractor.

axiom_nodes.name: T16.1 — Christianity 8 of 8 BCs
axiom_nodes.notes: The interview is broadly Christian-apologetic but never engages the boundary-condition scorecard.

axiom_nodes.name: T16.4 — Buddhism Fails BC1
axiom_nodes.notes: Habermas mentions he nearly became a Buddhist and that Buddhism is sometimes claimed to provide a metaphysical background for physics, but he does not evaluate Buddhism against BC1.

axiom_nodes.name: T16.6 — Atheism Fails BC1-BC6
axiom_nodes.notes: Atheism and skepticism are discussed as scholarly positions, but not assessed against the boundary conditions.

axiom_nodes.name: PERSONHOOD — Agency, Intentionality, Relational Capacity
axiom_nodes.notes: The source treats scholars and historical figures as agents with intentions and relationships, but does not assert the personhood axiom.

axiom_nodes.name: BRIDGE-PHY-THEO - Physics-Theology Bridge
axiom_nodes.notes: Habermas briefly mentions the claim that Buddhism provides a metaphysical background for physics, but he does not develop or endorse a physics-theology bridge.

axiom_nodes.name: U3 — Grace Universal
axiom_nodes.notes: Grace is invoked only in the ordinary interpersonal sense, not as a universal principle.

axiom_nodes.name: U4 — Fruits Universal
axiom_nodes.notes: The practical fruits of resurrection belief are discussed, but not as the canon's fruits universal.

axiom_nodes.name: F1 — Love Measurement Domain
axiom_nodes.notes: Love of God and neighbor are cited as commands, but not as a measurement domain.

axiom_nodes.name: F7 — Faithfulness Measurement Domain
axiom_nodes.notes: Faith/belief is discussed as a scholarly stance, not as a measurable fruit.

axiom_nodes.name: F9 — Self-Control Measurement Domain
axiom_nodes.notes: Anger and charity in debate are discussed, but not as self-control measurement.
